name: Afghanistan
system_note: An unrecognised Islamic emirate ruled by decree from Kandahar.
snapshot: Pakistan bombed Kabul and Kandahar in 2026 and declared "open war" on the Taliban, accusing it of sheltering militants who attack Pakistani soldiers.
culture: Afghanistan sits at the crossroads of Persian, Central Asian and South Asian civilisations. Dari and Pashto are the main languages, and poetry, from Rumi, who was born in Balkh, to the landays sung by Pashtun women, is deeply loved. The Taliban have banned most music, destroyed instruments and restricted cricket and other sports for women, though men's cricket remains a national passion.
society: Since retaking power in 2021, the Taliban have barred girls from school beyond sixth grade and women from universities, most jobs, parks and gyms, a system the UN calls gender apartheid. Foreign aid cuts in 2025 closed clinics, and millions of Afghans have been forced back from Iran and Pakistan. Opium poppy cultivation fell sharply after a Taliban ban.
situation: For 20 years, Pakistan's military intelligence sheltered the Afghan Taliban as they fought the Americans, betting that a Taliban government in Kabul would be a friendly one. When the Taliban took power in 2021, Pakistani officials celebrated. Five years later, the two are at war, and the bet has become what analysts call strategic blowback.

The cause is the Pakistani Taliban (TTP), an allied but separate movement that has escalated attacks inside Pakistan since 2021 from bases Islamabad says are in Afghanistan. After border clashes in October 2025, Qatar and Turkey brokered a ceasefire, but talks failed to make it last. On 22 February 2026 Pakistan struck seven alleged TTP camps; the Taliban retaliated against Pakistani border posts in six provinces, claiming 55 soldiers killed. On 27 February Pakistan bombed Kabul, Kandahar and Paktia, its widest bombardment of the capital and its first strikes on Kandahar, the Taliban's southern power base, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif declared: "Now it is open war between us and you" (AFP via The New Arab). The Taliban, with no air force to speak of, answered with drone strikes on Pakistani bases and said it wanted dialogue. The war came on top of a humanitarian emergency: Pakistan and Iran have expelled millions of Afghan refugees since 2023, women remain barred from secondary school and most work, and foreign aid has collapsed. Russia remains the only country to formally recognise the Taliban government.
power: An unrecognised Islamic emirate. Supreme leader Hibatullah Akhundzada rules by decree from Kandahar, with a cabinet in Kabul and no constitution, legislature or elections. Policy follows his interpretation of Islamic law.
holders: Supreme Leader Hibatullah Akhundzada; acting Prime Minister Mohammad Hasan Akhund.
